What you get

Showcase

Share your film. Made something with video-shotcraft? Submit it with the Showcase issue form. After review it appears on the Showcase page.

Requirements

Needs For
Node.js and npm Remotion rendering, the template and the workbench
ffmpeg / ffprobe Frame checks and final QA
uv Only for BGM beat analysis (runs a one-off Python script)
puppeteer Only for page capture; the capture script installs it on demand

Remotion downloads its own headless Chrome on first render. Tested on macOS; Linux works with the notes below.

Headless Linux / CI notes

Rendering on a headless Linux box (tested: 2 cores, Node 22) hits three walls:

  1. Concurrency cap. remotion still/render fails with "Maximum for --concurrency is 2" on low-core machines. Pass --concurrency=1.
  2. Old headless removal. Recent Chrome/Chromium dropped the old headless mode, so pointing Remotion at system Chromium fails to launch. Use a chrome-headless-shell binary instead of full Chrome.
  3. Blocked CDN. If remotion.media is unreachable (common in mainland China), the automatic headless-shell download fails. Pass --browser-executable=<path-to-local chrome-headless-shell>.

With these three flags, frame renders from the bundled template work.

Repository structure 
video-shotcraft/
├── SKILL.md                 # Agent entry point and core production rules
├── references/
│   ├── pipeline.md          # End-to-end production workflow
│   ├── shots/               # 124 shot recipe cards in 10 functional categories
│   ├── sequences/           # Reusable full-video structures and sequence patterns
│   ├── aesthetic-rules.md   # Visual QA criteria
│   ├── music-beat-sync.md   # BGM analysis and beat-sync methodology
│   ├── sound-design.md      # Sound-design guidance and examples
│   ├── sfx-sourcing.md      # Freesound search, download, analysis and credits
│   ├── jianying-export.md   # JianYing (CapCut CN) project-export guide
│   ├── publish-upload-post.md # Optional social publishing (Upload-Post API)
│   └── workbench.md         # Motion workbench: manifest contract + editability rules
├── demos/                   # Remotion reference implementations (same categories)
├── gallery/                 # Static motion-preview Gallery
├── template/                # Runnable complete video template
├── jianying-export/         # JianYing draft installers (mac tested / win untested)
├── publish/                 # Optional social publisher (stdlib-only Python) + offline tests
├── workbench/               # Post-delivery motion workbench (Vite + Remotion Player)
└── assets/
    ├── lib/                 # Reusable Remotion components
    ├── scripts/             # Page capture + Freesound CLI and offline tests
    └── audio/
        └── bgm/             # 5 BGM options; SFX downloaded per project

For the full workflow see SKILL.md, the production pipeline and the visual QA criteria.

Audio and assets

SFX come directly from Freesound, downloaded into each video's project. The shared SFX library has been removed. The sourcing guide covers search, CC0 / CC BY filtering, MP3 preview downloads, measurements and source/credit manifests. The Python CLI uses the standard library; downloading and analysis require FFmpeg. No API key is needed. Sound design covers timing and mixing. The template retains its fixed historical audio for playback and regression checks; new product videos source their SFX from Freesound. BGM options remain in assets/audio/bgm/.

Product screenshots bundled with the template are demonstration assets. Replace them with screenshots of your product before publishing, and check whether any product, customer or personal data needs to be anonymized.

License

  • Code and docs: Apache-2.0.
  • Freesound audio: each file under its recorded license; retain the project manifest and publish required CC BY credits.
  • BGM: see ATTRIBUTION.md. Historical template audio: see template credits.
  • Remotion has its own license: free for individuals and small teams, companies may need a paid license.

Acknowledgements

Many recipes were distilled by studying the motion language of outstanding official product films, including promos from ClickUp, Perplexity, Slack, Notion, Figma, Framer, Bear, Raycast, Pitch, Miro, Superhuman and Loom. The cards document techniques (timing, easing, choreography) re-implemented from scratch; no footage, artwork or brand assets from these films are included. All trademarks belong to their owners, and none of these companies are affiliated with or endorse this project.

The Freesound sourcing workflow was inspired by vibe-motion/sound. Thanks to its authors for sharing the approach of selecting sounds by source descriptions, duration, download counts, rating counts and licenses. Video Shotcraft's search/download CLI is independently implemented.

Thanks also to Remotion, which powers every demo and template here; Freesound and its contributors for project SFX; Mixkit for BGM and historical template audio; the game-feel and animation communities whose published principles inform several cards; and Claude Code, with which this library was built, iterated and QA'd using the same workflow the skill teaches.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An AI agent skill that transforms Claude Code and Codex into a programmatic motion-design video studio.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Video-shotcraft functions as an advanced AI agent skill that seamlessly transforms standard coding assistants, like Claude Code or Codex, into programmatic motion-design studios. It completely automates the complex pipeline of storyboarding, animating, and sound-designing cinematic product videos using purely text-based prompts. By deeply integrating the Remotion framework, it exposes a massive library of 152 specialized shot recipe cards and 209 precise motion styles directly to the AI model. This allows developers to programmatically instruct their AI to generate highly professional, production-ready marketing or demo videos in minutes.
keyFeatures: Agent integration: Operates as a direct skill for Claude Code and Codex, enabling complex video generation within standard AI workflows.
Extensive shot library: Empowers the AI with 152 distinct shot recipe cards to guide accurate and engaging scene storyboarding.
Precise motion styling: Provides the AI with 209 specific motion previews and styles to ensure dynamic, professional visual animations.
Programmatic rendering: Leverages the Remotion framework to natively render high-quality, cinematic video content using modern web technologies.
Production-ready templates: Supplies fully pre-configured templates that allow the AI to quickly output polished promotional marketing content.
